([[High Point, North Carolina]]) | college = [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] (2018–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 55 | draft_team = [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2026|start}} | team1 = [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–[[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team2 = →[[Oklahoma City Blue]] | years3 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team3 = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ({{nbafy|2025}}) * [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Sixth Man of the Year (2020) }} '''Aaron Daniel Wiggins''' (born January 2, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]], where he was named [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Sixth Man of the Year in 2020. Wiggins was selected by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]]. Spending five seasons with the team, he won an NBA championship with the Thunder in [[2025 NBA Finals|2025]]. He was traded to the Hawks during the 2026 off-season. ==Early life== Wiggins grew up playing basketball, [[American football|football]] and running [[track and field|track]]. Through his childhood, he played the [[piano]] and [[trombone]], acted in plays and danced.{{cite news |last1=Giambalvo |first1=Emily |title=Maryland's Aaron Wiggins knows tap, jazz, ballet and hip-hop. |url-status=live }} He had drawn the attention of Maryland's coaching staff while they were visiting Wesleyan to watch his teammate [[Jaylen Hoard]]. ==College career== [[File:Aaron Wiggins with Maryland.png|thumb|left|150px|Wiggins with Maryland in 2021]] Wiggins began his freshman season as a starter, but later told coach [[Mark Turgeon]] that he was more comfortable coming off the bench. As a freshman at Maryland, he played the most minutes among his team's reserves.{{cite web |last1=DuBose |first1=Brooks |title=Maryland Basketball's Aaron Wiggins A Bench Player In Name Only |url-status=live }} In the final game of his junior season, Wiggins scored a career-high 27 points in a 96–77 loss to [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] in the second round of the |url-status=live }} As a junior, he averaged 14.5 points, 5.8 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game, earning All-Big Ten honorable mention. On April 9, 2021, Wiggins declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Giambalvo |first1=Emily |title=Maryland's Aaron Wiggins, Eric Ayala declare for NBA draft while maintaining eligibility |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/04/09/aaron-wiggins-nba-draft/ |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=April 9, 2021 |archive-date=May 14, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210514021451/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/04/09/aaron-wiggins-nba-draft/ |url-status=live }} He later decided to remain in the draft.{{cite web |last1=Oyefusi |first1=Daniel |title=Maryland guard Aaron Wiggins keeping name in NBA draft, will forgo senior season |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2021/07/05/maryland-guard-aaron-wiggins-keeping-name-in-nba-draft-will-forgo-senior-season/ |website=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=July 5, 2021 |archive-date=July 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210726230059/https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/bs-sp-maryland-aaron-wiggins-nba-draft-20210705-jhl6ufsqazfmxjrszicgxhrmf4-story.html |url-status=live }} ==Professional career== === Oklahoma City Thunder (2021–2026) === Wiggins was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 55th pick by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. Wiggins had a very productive [[NBA Summer League]] with the Thunder averaging the second most points on the team with 11.2 PPG.{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Ermann|title=Aaron Wiggins, former Maryland {{sic|baske|ball|hide=y}} standout, taken in NBA Draft|url=https://247sports.com/college/maryland/Article/Aaron-Wiggins-former-Maryland-baskeball-standout-taken-in-NBA-Draft-168464042/|website=247 Sports.com|date=July 29, 2021|access-date=August 3, 2021|archive-date=July 30, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210730185901/https://247sports.com/college/maryland/Article/Aaron-Wiggins-former-Maryland-baskeball-standout-taken-in-NBA-Draft-168464042/|url-status=live}} On August 15, 2021, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Thunder. Under the terms of the deal, he split time between the Thunder and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Aaron Wiggins to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-wiggins-210815|website=NBA.com|date=August 15, 2021|access-date=September 3, 2021|archive-date=August 24, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210824231605/https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-wiggins-210815|url-status=live}} On December 26, 2021, Wiggins scored a then career-high 24 points against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. He shot 8 for 10 from the field and 2 for 4 from three in Thunder's 117–112 win. On February 12, 2022, the Thunder converted Wiggins two-way contract into a standard NBA deal.{{cite web|title=Thunder Rookie Aaron Wiggins Signed to Full-Time NBA Deal|url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/thunder-rookie-aaron-wiggins-signed-to-full-time-nba-deal|website=SI.com|date=February 12, 2022|access-date=February 12, 2022|archive-date=February 14, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220214235514/https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/thunder-rookie-aaron-wiggins-signed-to-full-time-nba-deal|url-status=live}} On July 7, 2024, Wiggins re-signed with the Thunder on a five-year, $45 million contract.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Aaron Wiggins to Multi-Year Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/aaron-wiggins-240707|website=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2024|access-date=July 15, 2024}} On February 1, 2025, Wiggins registered a career-high 41 points and 14 rebounds against the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{Cite web |date=2025-02-02 |title=Aaron Wiggins, Dominant First Half Fuel 144-110 Win Over Kings |url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/aaron-wiggins-dominates-kings-okc-win |access-date=2025-02-02 |website=Oklahoma City Thunder On SI |language=en-US}} Wiggins became an [[NBA champion]] when the Thunder defeated the [[Indiana Pacers]] in game 7 of the [[2025 NBA Finals]].{{cite web | last=Ermann | first=Jeff | title=Aaron Wiggins wins NBA championship ring, joining surprisingly small group of Terps and ending 20-year drought | website=247Sports | date=2025-06-23 | url=https://247sports.com/college/maryland/article/aaron-wiggins-wins-nba-championship-ring-joining-surprisingly-small-group-of-terps-and-ending-20-year-drought-251173370/ | access-date=2025-12-07}}
